data.name: Dash_QuickScan_Tip
data.value: Choose an NTFS, FAT32 or exFAT drive, then press Quick Scan on its card.

data.name: Dash_DeepScan_Tip
data.value: Choose a drive, then press Deep Scan on its card. Searches the drive's data for file signatures; works on NTFS, FAT32 and exFAT.

data.name: Dash_ScanNote
data.value: Quick Scan reads the drive's file records (NTFS, FAT32, exFAT) and keeps original names and folders. Deep Scan searches the raw data for known file types (photos, videos, documents, audio, archives) on any drive, including formatted ones, but cannot recover original names.

data.name: Tip_1
data.value: Stop using the affected drive immediately after data loss to reduce the risk of overwriting.

data.name: Tip_2
data.value: Never recover files onto the same drive you are scanning.

data.name: Tip_3
data.value: Recovery is not guaranteed. Overwritten data may be unrecoverable.

data.name: Tip_4
data.value: SSD TRIM can make deleted data impossible to recover.

data.name: Tip_5
data.value: Encrypted storage may prevent recovery; physically damaged drives may need a professional lab.

data.name: Drives_Subtitle
data.value: Detected drives. Reading drive details is read-only and never modifies your data.

data.name: Drives_None
data.value: No fixed or removable drives were detected.

data.name: Drives_Failed
data.value: Drive detection failed. See the log for details.

data.name: Drive_Scan_Tip
data.value: Looks for deleted files in the drive's own file records (NTFS, FAT32, exFAT) and keeps their names and folders. Read-only; needs administrator rights.

data.name: Drive_Verify_Tip
data.value: Opens the drive read-only and reads its first sector. Needs administrator rights.

data.name: Warn_Trim
data.value: SSD with TRIM enabled: deleted files may be permanently erased and unrecoverable.

data.name: Warn_SsdNoTrim
data.value: SSD / flash media: recovery chances are usually lower than on a hard disk.

data.name: Verify_Confirm_Body
data.value: RecoverX will open {0} read-only and read its first sector to identify the file system. Nothing is written to the drive. Continue?

data.name: Verify_Success
Verify_Denied
data.value: Windows denied access to {0}. Raw drive access requires administrator rights. Restart RecoverX as administrator to verify.

data.name: Verify_NotFound
data.value: {0} could not be found. It may have been removed.

data.name: Verify_EngineMissing
data.value: The native engine is not loaded, so read access cannot be verified. Reason: {0}

data.name: Admin_Banner
data.value: RecoverX is not running as administrator. Reading drives at the raw level needs administrator rights.

data.name: Admin_Confirm_Body
data.value: RecoverX will close and reopen with administrator rights. Windows will ask you to approve this. Continue?

data.name: Hist_Subtitle
data.value: Previous scan sessions. A session can only be resumed when its scan state can be safely reconstructed.

data.name: Hist_Clear_Confirm
data.value: Delete all {0} scan history entries? This cannot be undone.

data.name: Hist_LoadFailed
data.value: Could not load scan history. See the log for details.

data.name: Set_Destination_Note
data.value: Optional. Use a different drive than the one you are recovering from.

data.name: Set_Dest_Invalid
data.value: That folder does not exist. Enter a full path to an existing folder.

data.name: Set_Dest_Unsafe
data.value: This folder is on {0}. Never use it as the destination when recovering files from that drive.

data.name: Set_Dest_Unverified
data.value: RecoverX could not confirm which drive this folder is on. Make sure it is not on the drive you recover from.

data.name: Set_ScanPrefs_Note
data.value: File categories and the minimum size hide results you do not want; they never change what is read from the drive.

data.name: Set_Categories_Note
data.value: Choose which kinds of files scans should report. Extensions are comma-separated, without dots.

data.name: Set_Cat_Invalid
data.value: {0}: use only letters and digits in extensions, separated by commas, with at least one extension.

data.name: Set_Cat_CatchAll
data.value: Everything not matched by the other categories.

data.name: Set_Preview_Formats
data.value: Preview formats: JPG, JPEG, PNG, BMP, GIF (image), TXT and similar text files (first 64 KB), PDF (document details and a text sample; pages are not rendered).

data.name: Set_Preview_Note
data.value: Previews read the file's data from the drive (read-only) when you select it. Damaged files may preview incorrectly or not at all.

data.name: Set_History_Max
data.value: Keep at most this many scan history entries

data.name: Set_Prefs_Invalid
data.value: Enter whole numbers within the allowed ranges (file size 0-{0} KB, preview 1-{1} MB, history {2}-{3} entries).

data.name: Set_OpenLogs_Failed
data.value: Could not open the logs folder.

data.name: Set_SaveFailed
data.value: Settings could not be saved. See the log for details.

data.name: About_Status
data.value: Phase 5 build: Quick Scan for NTFS, FAT32 and exFAT (original names and folders), Deep Scan (file signatures, free space only on these file systems), search and filters, file preview, and safe recovery.

data.name: About_Limits
data.value: Recovery is never guaranteed. Overwritten data may be unrecoverable, SSD TRIM can permanently erase deleted data, encrypted storage may prevent recovery, and physically damaged drives may need professional recovery.

data.name: About_Compat
data.value: Compatibility with Windows 7 SP1, 10 and 11 is not claimed until it has been tested on those systems.

data.name: Drive_Scan_NotNtfs
data.value: Quick Scan supports NTFS, FAT32 and exFAT drives. Use Deep Scan for this drive.

data.name: Scan_Idle
data.value: Choose a drive on the Drive Scan page and press Quick Scan or Deep Scan.

data.name: Scan_Phase_Validating
data.value: Checking which files can be recovered...

data.name: Scan_Confirm_Body
data.value: RecoverX will read the file records of {0} (read-only) to look for deleted files. Nothing is written to the drive. Continue?

data.name: Scan_Hidden_Filters
data.value: {0} file(s) hidden by your Settings (file categories and minimum size).

data.name: Scan_Truncated
data.value: Listing stopped after {0} files. Narrow the file categories or raise the minimum size in Settings and scan again.

data.name: Scan_Cancelled
data.value: Scan cancelled. The results below were found before cancelling and may be incomplete.

data.name: Scan_Failed
data.value: The scan could not be completed: {0}

data.name: Scan_BitmapMissing
data.value: The drive's cluster map could not be read, so overwritten files cannot be detected. Treat every result with caution.

data.name: Scan_MftPartial
data.value: The file table is fragmented in a way this version cannot fully follow, so some files may be missing.

data.name: Scan_Err_Denied
data.value: Windows denied access to {0}. Scanning needs administrator rights. Use "Restart as administrator" on the Drive Scan page.

data.name: Scan_Err_NotNtfs
data.value: {0} cannot be read as NTFS, FAT32 or exFAT. It may use another file system, be encrypted (for example with BitLocker), or be damaged. Try Deep Scan, which does not need the file system.

data.name: Scan_Err_Corrupt
data.value: The NTFS structures on {0} are too damaged to read.

data.name: Scan_Err_Engine
data.value: The native engine is not available: {0}

data.name: Scan_Err_NotFound
data.value: {0} could not be found. It may have been removed.

data.name: Scan_DestinationHint
data.value: Choose a folder on a different drive than {0}. RecoverX creates a new folder inside it and never overwrites existing files.

data.name: CondTip_Verified
data.value: The data area is unused and the file header matches its type.

data.name: CondTip_Likely
data.value: The data area is unused. The file type could not be verified.

data.name: CondTip_Partial
data.value: {0} of {1} clusters are now used by other files. Recovered data will be incomplete.

data.name: CondTip_Lost
data.value: The data area has been reused, or the content no longer matches the file type.

data.name: CondTip_Unsupported
data.value: Compressed, encrypted or otherwise unsupported data cannot be recovered yet.

data.name: CondTip_Empty
data.value: The file had no content. Only its name and dates can be restored.

data.name: CondTip_Unknown
data.value: RecoverX could not assess this file.

data.name: Recover_Confirm_Body
Recover_Confirm_Risky
data.value: {0} of the selected files are likely damaged or incomplete (partly overwritten, or their content does not match their type). They will be recovered but flagged.

data.name: Recover_Done
data.value: Recovery finished: {0} recovered, {1} need attention, {2} could not be recovered.

data.name: Recover_Cancelled
data.value: Recovery cancelled. Files already recovered are kept.

data.name: Recover_Err_DestInvalid
data.value: The recovery folder does not exist.

data.name: Recover_Err_SameVolume
data.value: The recovery folder is on {0}, the drive being recovered. Choose a folder on a different drive.

data.name: Recover_Err_Unverifiable
data.value: RecoverX cannot confirm which drive this folder is on. Choose a folder on a normal drive letter, for example D:\Recovered.

data.name: Recover_Err_Space
data.value: Not enough free space in the recovery folder: {0} needed, {1} available.

data.name: Recover_Err_Create
data.value: The recovery folder could not be created: {0}

data.name: Out_Unverified
data.value: Recovered - size correct, content type not verifiable

data.name: Out_Suspect
data.value: Recovered, but content may be damaged: {0}

data.name: Out_Unsupported
data.value: Not recovered: compressed or encrypted files are not supported yet

data.name: Reason_HeaderMismatch
data.value: the file header does not match its type

data.name: Reason_PartlyOverwritten
data.value: part of its data area was reused by other files

data.name: Reason_Overwritten
data.value: its data area was reused or no longer matches

data.name: Reason_ShortRead
data.value: fewer bytes could be read than the file size

data.name: Reason_ReadError
data.value: the data could not be read

data.name: Reason_WriteError
data.value: the file could not be written

data.name: Reason_RecordReused
data.value: the file table entry has been reused since the scan

data.name: Rec_Subtitle
data.value: Files recovered with RecoverX. Only this list is cleared by "Clear list"; the recovered files stay where they are.

data.name: Rec_None
data.value: No files have been recovered yet.

data.name: Rec_Clear_Confirm
data.value: Remove all {0} entries from this list? The recovered files themselves are not deleted.

data.name: Rec_Load_Failed
data.value: Could not load the list. See the log for details.

data.name: Drive_DeepScan_Tip
data.value: Searches the drive's data for known file types (photos, videos, documents, audio, archives). Works on any file system, also after formatting. Read-only; needs administrator rights. Can take a long time on large drives.

data.name: Deep_Confirm_Body
data.value: RecoverX will read {0} ({1}) sector by sector (read-only) and look for known file types. Nothing is written to the drive. On NTFS, FAT32 and exFAT only free space is searched; otherwise the whole drive is read. This can take a long time; you can pause or stop it and keep what was found. Continue?

data.name: Deep_TimeNote
data.value: Deep Scan reads every searched sector of the drive. Pause frees the drive for a while; Stop keeps the files found so far.

data.name: Deep_AllSpace
data.value: Space used by existing files was searched too (Settings), so results can include files that were never deleted.

data.name: Deep_NoMapNtfs
data.value: The drive's free-space map could not be read, so the whole drive was searched. Results can include files that still exist.

data.name: Deep_NoMap
data.value: The drive's file system could not be read, so the whole drive was searched. Results can include files that still exist.

data.name: Deep_ReadErrors
data.value: {0} region(s) of the drive could not be read and were skipped. The drive may be failing; consider a professional service before using it further.

data.name: Deep_Contiguous
data.value: Deep Scan cannot recover original file names or folders. It assumes each file is stored in one piece: fragmented or partly overwritten files are rated Partial or Poor, never Excellent.

data.name: Deep_Summary
data.value: Deep Scan found {0} file(s) by signature on {1}.

data.name: Scan_Summary_All
data.value: Quick Scan found {0} deleted file(s) on {1}.

data.name: Scan_Paused
data.value: Paused. The drive is not being read.

data.name: Scan_StopKeep_Tip
data.value: Stops the scan and shows the files found so far.

data.name: Scan_Browse_Title
data.value: Choose the folder to recover files into. It must be on a different drive than the one being recovered.

data.name: Rating_Estimate
data.value: Ratings are estimates based on what could be checked on the drive. They do not guarantee that a recovered file will open.

data.name: CarveTip_Checksum
data.value: Found by signature. Its structure was followed to its end and its checksums match.

data.name: CarveTip_Verified
data.value: Found by signature. Its structure was followed from the header to the end marker without errors.

data.name: CarveTip_Likely
data.value: Found by signature. Its size is known, but its content could not be fully checked.

data.name: CarveTip_Partial
data.value: Found by signature, but its structure breaks part-way (fragmented or partly overwritten). Only the part that checked out will be recovered.

data.name: CarveTip_Truncated
data.value: Found by signature, but it runs past the end of the drive or the size limit. The recovered file will be incomplete.

data.name: CarveTip_Lost
data.value: Only the file's header could be confirmed.

data.name: CarveTip_InUse
data.value: {0} of {1} clusters it covers now belong to existing files, so part of the data may have been overwritten.

data.name: CarveTip_InUseChecksum
data.value: {0} of {1} clusters it covers are marked in use, but all checksums still match, so the data is intact.

data.name: Preview_Hint
data.value: Select a file to preview it. Images (JPG, PNG, BMP, GIF), PDF and any text file are shown; other files show their first bytes. Dates marked * come from inside the file (photo or video).

data.name: Preview_Loading
data.value: Reading the file from the drive...

data.name: Preview_NotSupported
data.value: No preview is available for this file type.

data.name: Preview_DamagedWarning
data.value: This file may be damaged. The preview shows the data as it was found.

data.name: Preview_DecodeFailed
data.value: The image could not be displayed. Its data may be damaged or incomplete.

data.name: Preview_Disabled
data.value: Preview is turned off in Settings.

data.name: Preview_TooLarge
data.value: This file ({0}) is larger than the preview limit in Settings.

data.name: Preview_NoData
data.value: This file has no data that can be read.

data.name: Preview_ReadFailed
data.value: The file could not be read for preview: {0}

data.name: Preview_Pdf_Encrypted
data.value: The document is encrypted; its text cannot be shown.

data.name: Preview_Pdf_TextHeader
data.value: Text found in the document (layout not shown):

data.name: Preview_Pdf_NoText
data.value: No readable text was found (the PDF may contain only images, or use embedded font encodings).

data.name: Set_ScanType_Note
data.value: The default scan is listed first on each drive card.

data.name: Set_DeepAllSpace
data.value: Deep Scan: also search space used by existing files

data.name: Set_DeepAllSpace_Note
data.value: Off: only free space is searched, so existing files are not listed. On: slower, and results include files that were never deleted.

data.name: Preview_Erased
data.value: The data of this file ({0}) reads back as all zeros: it was erased, usually by SSD TRIM after deletion, or overwritten with zeros. There is nothing left to preview, and the recovered file will be empty.

data.name: Preview_HexHeader
data.value: No viewer for this content. First bytes of the file (hex):

data.name: Preview_TypeMismatch
data.value: The name says {0}, but the content is not a {0} file. It may have been overwritten, or it is not what its name suggests.

data.name: Scan_NameGuessed
data.value: First letter of the name was lost on deletion (shown as _)

data.name: Scan_Err_NotFat
data.value: {0} cannot be read as FAT32 or exFAT. It may be damaged. Try Deep Scan, which does not need the file system.

data.name: Fat_Contiguous
data.value: FAT32 erases a deleted file's list of clusters, so RecoverX reads each file as one continuous piece. Files that were stored in pieces (fragmented) may be rated Partial or come back damaged; check them with Preview.

data.name: Drive_Snapshots_Tip
data.value: Looks for deleted files in Windows restore points (shadow copies) of this drive. Works even on SSDs with TRIM, if a restore point was made before the file was deleted. Read-only; needs administrator rights.

data.name: Drive_Snapshots_NotNtfs
data.value: Windows keeps restore points only for NTFS drives.

data.name: Snap_Confirm_Body
data.value: RecoverX will compare the Windows restore points (shadow copies) of {0} with the drive and list files that existed in a restore point but are gone now. Nothing is changed. System folders, program folders and AppData are skipped. Continue?

data.name: Snap_Phase
data.value: Comparing restore points with the drive...

data.name: Snap_Found
data.value: {0} deleted files found in restore points so far

data.name: Snap_None
data.value: Windows has no restore points for {0}, so there is nothing to search. (System Protection may be turned off for this drive. For the future, turn it on in Control Panel > System > System Protection, or use File History / OneDrive.)

data.name: Snap_NotSupported
data.value: Windows keeps restore points only for NTFS drives; {0} is not NTFS.

data.name: Snap_Info
data.value: Searched {0} restore point(s). Each file is an exact copy of the file as it was when that restore point was made; the newest copy is listed. System, program and AppData folders were skipped.

data.name: Snap_Unreadable
data.value: {0} folder(s) in restore points could not be read and were skipped.

data.name: Snap_Summary
data.value: Found {0} file(s) in restore points of {1} that no longer exist on the drive.

data.name: Snap_Tip
data.value: Copied from a Windows restore point made {0}. The file is intact as of that moment; later changes to it are not included.
